title: Eye redness, eye pain, photophobia and blurred vision: suspect acute uveitis — seek ophthalmology care promptly
summary: The most common ocular complication of AS is acute anterior uveitis (eye redness / eye pain / photophobia / blurred vision); ophthalmology review is needed the same day or the next day, and prompt treatment prevents posterior synechiae.
applicable_scene: symptom_daily eye symptom checkboxes; emergency centre scenario card; checkup_items ophthalmology periodic item overdue reminder
source_name: Gupta N, Agarwal A. Management of Uveitis in Spondyloarthropathy: Current Trends (PMC5741284, The Permanente Journal); Iatrox UKMLA Anterior Uveitis clinical material

payload.urgency: seek ophthalmology care the same day or the next day (UKMLA: Same-day or next-day ophthalmology referral)
steps: Recognise the symptoms (the four cardinal signs) — this card appears the moment the eye symptom checkboxes in this APP are ticked
Stop the current activity and avoid bright light (wear sunglasses for relief when photophobic)
Attend ophthalmology the same day or the next day (eye emergency or uveitis specialist clinic)
Tell the doctor about the AS history and current medications (topical corticosteroid treatment must follow a full, standard course — do not stop it on your own)
After the visit: log the event (emergency_events) + set a follow-up reminder
red_flag: Severe, intense pain / sudden drop in vision — seek immediate medical care at the emergency department (ED) (not the next day)
Risk of delay: posterior synechiae -> pupil block -> secondary glaucoma (UKMLA)
Recurrent episodes should be reported to rheumatology (they may be related to disease activity — a topic for the follow-up visit)
payload.app_link: emergency card uveitis rendering; symptom_daily eye field trigger; checkup_items(eye) periodic item; emergency_events logging

title: Fever or signs of infection: biologic therapy users should contact their doctor — do not self-administer the next dose
summary: Contact your doctor promptly if you have fever, a persistent cough, red swollen painful skin, or flu-like symptoms; for serious infection or sepsis the doctor will stop the biologic — this is not a matter of self-discontinuing the drug.
applicable_scene: vitals.temperature ≥ 38.5 (threshold item linkage); symptom_daily.feverish=1; fever on an injection day (itx-002 linkage)
source_name: FDA Enbrel label; EMA Inflectra product information (EMA EPAR, https://www.ema.europa.eu/en/medicines/human/EPAR/inflectra , HTTP 200 verified); Inflectra patient information (Pfizer, ⚠️ specific URL unverified)

symptoms: red, swollen, warm and painful skin
payload.urgency: Signs of infection appear -> contact your doctor the same day; high fever / altered mental status -> emergency department (ED)
steps: Measure and record body temperature (vitals) — ≥38.5 automatically brings up this card

Biologic therapy users: contact your treating physician before the next injection date (whether to delay is the doctor's decision — do not self-administer the next dose, and do not decide on your own to stop permanently)
Review exposure history over the past 2 weeks (colds / infection in family members / travel) and tell your doctor
After the visit: log emergency_events + medication pause status (medication_changes: pause, source=hospital)
red_flag: Persistent high fever / chills / confusion — seek immediate medical care at the emergency department (ED)
Signs of infection during biologic therapy may be partly masked (immunosuppressed state, so symptoms may not match infection severity) — judge conservatively

FDA/EMA position: treatment should be stopped if serious infection or sepsis develops (Enbrel: should be discontinued if a patient develops a serious infection or sepsis) — the decision to stop rests with the doctor
payload.app_link: threshold linkage (edu-th-001); itx-002 black box linkage; injection card fever-day prompt; medication_changes(pause) quick logging

title: After a fall, seek medical assessment even if you "feel fine": vertebral fractures in AS are easily missed
summary: Spinal stiffness in AS plus osteoporosis means a low-energy fall can cause a fracture, and it is often missed and diagnosis delayed; those with cervical spine involvement need particular caution, and do not move the neck yourself after a fall.
applicable_scene: emergency centre scenario card; emergency_events(fall_fracture) logging; pinned prompt for users with profile.spine_mobility≥moderate
source_name: Chaudhary SB et al. Management of Acute Spinal Fractures in Ankylosing Spondylitis (PMC3263739)

symptoms: new pain in the neck / back / lower back after a fall
numbness or weakness in the limbs
feeling fine yet AS fractures are often painless and asymmetrical
payload.urgency: After a fall, always seek medical assessment (even without clear pain); neck pain / limb numbness — emergency department (ED)
steps: After a fall do not get up or move yourself (first check limb sensation and movement yourself)
If the cervical spine is involved, keep the neck in a neutral position and wait for the ambulance (a traditional collar may worsen the injury — immobilise only after specialist assessment)
Proactively tell the doctor about the AS history ("I have ankylosing spondylitis, my spine is fragile, please take X-rays" — what the patient says is key to preventing a missed diagnosis)
After the visit: log emergency_events + imaging results (lab_results attachment path can be linked)
red_flag: Severe neck pain / numbness or weakness in the limbs / bladder and bowel dysfunction — seek immediate medical care at the emergency department (ED), do not move the patient
AS fracture diagnosis frequently missed or delayed (source text) — "feels fine" is not a valid basis for judgement
Traditional collars may cause hyperextension through the fracture site and worsen the injury (Traditional collars may cause hyperextension through the fracture site) — do not put on a collar yourself
payload.app_link: emergency card fall_fracture rendering; spine_mobility user pinning; emergency_events logging

title: Numbness or weakness in the lower limbs / bladder and bowel dysfunction: suspect cauda equina syndrome — seek emergency care
summary: A rare but well-defined neurological complication of long-standing AS; progressive numbness and weakness in the lower limbs, bladder and bowel dysfunction, or abnormal perineal sensation (saddle anaesthesia) should prompt emergency assessment as soon as possible — do not wait and do not observe.
applicable_scene: symptom_daily neurological symptom checkboxes (new red-flag fields); emergency centre scenario card
source_name: J Rheumatol review "Cauda Equina Syndrome in Ankylosing Spondylitis: Challenges in Diagnosis, Management, and Pathogenesis" (2019;46(12):1582-1588, PMID 30936280, DOI 10.3899/jrheum.181259 — **fully matches** the volume, issue and page numbers linked for this entry) — ⚠️ the original source name listed "Ann Rheum Dis 神经并发症综述" (Ann Rheum Dis review of neurological complications) first, but the link points to J Rheumatol, so **the first item and the link are not the same article**; this has been corrected

symptoms: progressive numbness and weakness in the lower limbs
payload.urgency: emergency department (ED) (red-flag symptom level — rare but must not be delayed)
steps: Recognise the triad of symptoms (the appearance of any one triggers this card)
Seek immediate medical care at the emergency department (ED) (neurosurgery / spine surgery assessment) — do not adopt a watch-and-wait approach
Tell the doctor about the AS history (CES is a known association in long-standing AS, which helps the doctor localise the problem)
Log emergency_events
red_flag: Bladder and bowel dysfunction + saddle anaesthesia are classic indications for emergency care — waiting means delay
CES has a major impact on quality of life (J Rheumatol: extremely important effect on physical function and quality of life)
payload.note: Rare-complication educational framing: presented as a red-flag symptom entry, not rendered as a common symptom (to avoid anxiety) — placed in the "seek immediate medical care" section of the symptom checkbox page
payload.app_link: symptom_daily neurological red-flag field trigger; fourth scenario card in the emergency centre; cross-linked with the emr-003 fall entry (if neurological symptoms appear after a fall, this entry takes priority)

title: Long-term corticosteroids must not be stopped abruptly on your own: risk of adrenal insufficiency
summary: Corticosteroid use for more than 3–4 weeks can suppress the HPA axis, and abrupt cessation carries a risk of adrenal insufficiency and even adrenal crisis (fatigue / nausea / low blood pressure); if you have missed doses for several days or stopped the drug on your own and then feel unwell, seek medical care.
applicable_scene: medication_changes discontinuation logging (corticosteroid class with source other than hospital); alert for corticosteroid users who have missed doses for more than 2 days
source_name: Aust Prescr practical guidance on withdrawing corticosteroids (PMC12378006); Endocrine Society guideline on adrenal insufficiency (https://www.endocrine.org/clinical-practice-guidelines/adrenal-insufficiency , 302 redirect verified as reachable)

payload.urgency: Symptoms after missing doses for several days -> seek medical care the same day; severe (signs of shock) -> emergency department (ED)
steps: Long-term (>3–4 weeks) corticosteroid users who miss ≥2 days -> this card appears automatically (reminder to contact the doctor about a replacement dosing plan — do not double the dose on your own)
Self-discontinuation logged (source=patient) -> alert + recommendation to contact the doctor to agree a tapering plan
Symptom cluster appears -> tell the doctor "I have been on long-term corticosteroids and recently stopped" (key history information)
Log emergency_events / medication_changes
red_flag: Failure to recognise adrenal crisis can lead to shock and eventual death (Aust Prescr source text)

Short-term use within 3–4 weeks can be stopped abruptly / long-term use must be tapered (the source states this cut-off explicitly) — dose and duration are determined automatically from the medication list
Corticosteroid requirements may need to be increased under stress (surgery / infection / serious illness) — proactively report the corticosteroid history when seeking care
payload.app_link: medication_logs missed-dose count (corticosteroid class x 2 days trigger); medication_changes discontinuation source detection; cross-linked with the fdg-002 / emr-002 infection entries (stress dose increase scenario)
